description: Triage rules for Patient Intake Triage Assistant

rules.title: Low-grade fever, short duration, no red flags
follow_up_questions: What is the highest temperature you have recorded?
How many days have you had the fever?
Do you have any other symptoms like cough, sore throat, or body aches?
Are you taking any medications right now?
rules.reasoning: Low-grade fever (below 101°F) with short duration and no associated red flags can often be managed in primary care.

rules.title: Moderate fever with associated symptoms
follow_up_questions: What is the highest temperature you have recorded?
How long have you had the fever?
Do you have a stiff neck, rash, or difficulty breathing?
Have you traveled anywhere recently?
rules.reasoning: Moderate fever with associated symptoms requires evaluation in internal medicine to identify potential infection source.

rules.title: High fever with neurological or systemic red flags
follow_up_questions: What is your current temperature?
Are you experiencing confusion, stiff neck, or a rash?
Are you immunocompromised or on immunosuppressive medications?
rules.reasoning: High fever with neurological signs suggests possible serious infection requiring emergency evaluation.

rules.title: Fever - insufficient information for safe triage
follow_up_questions: Do you have a thermometer reading? What is the highest temperature?
When did the fever start?
Do you have any other symptoms?
rules.reasoning: Insufficient information to determine fever severity. Cannot safely apply a triage rule without basic temperature data.
escalation_conditions: patient unable to provide temperature information

rules.title: Minor injury with no red flags
follow_up_questions: How did the injury happen?
Where exactly is the pain?
Can you move the injured area?
Is there any swelling or bleeding?
rules.reasoning: Minor injury with full range of motion and no red flags can be managed in primary care or urgent care.

rules.title: Moderate injury requiring urgent evaluation
follow_up_questions: How did the injury happen?
Can you move the affected area normally?
Is the bleeding controlled?
Have you lost any sensation or movement?
When did the injury occur?
rules.reasoning: Injury with possible fracture or significant soft tissue damage requires urgent emergency evaluation.

rules.title: Head injury with concerning symptoms
follow_up_questions: Did you lose consciousness at any point?
Are you feeling confused or disoriented?
Do you have a severe headache, vomiting, or vision changes?
How did the head injury happen?
rules.reasoning: Head injury with neurological symptoms requires emergency evaluation to rule out intracranial injury.

rules.title: Injury - mechanism and severity unclear
follow_up_questions: Can you describe how the injury happened?
Where exactly are you experiencing pain or injury?
Are you able to move normally?
rules.reasoning: Insufficient information to determine injury severity. Cannot safely route without understanding mechanism and current status.
escalation_conditions: patient unable to describe the event

rules.title: Chest pain with cardiac red flags
red_flags: chest pain radiating to arm or jaw
shortness of breath with chest pain
sweating and nausea with chest pain
follow_up_questions: Can you describe the pain (sharp, dull, pressure, tightness)?
Does the pain spread to your arm, jaw, or back?
Are you experiencing shortness of breath, sweating, or nausea?
Do you have a history of heart problems or high blood pressure?
rules.reasoning: Chest pain with reported red-flag features requires urgent evaluation and human review.

rules.title: Chest pain without cardiac red flags
follow_up_questions: Can you describe the pain (sharp, dull, pressure)?
How long have you had the pain?
Does anything make it better or worse?
Do you have any shortness of breath or dizziness?
rules.reasoning: Chest pain without obvious cardiac red flags still requires emergency evaluation but may be lower acuity.
escalation_conditions: new onset chest pain in patient over 40
chest pain with unexplained weight loss

rules.title: Chest pain - information insufficient for safe triage
follow_up_questions: Can you describe the type of pain you are experiencing?
When did the chest pain start?
Are you having any difficulty breathing, sweating, or dizziness?
rules.reasoning: Chest pain requires thorough evaluation. Insufficient information to determine cardiac risk. Cannot safely apply a triage rule.
escalation_conditions: chest pain in patient over 50 with unknown history

rules.title: Severe respiratory distress with red flags
follow_up_questions: Can you speak in full sentences right now?
When did the breathing difficulty start?
Do you have a history of asthma, COPD, or other lung conditions?
Are your lips or fingernails discolored?
rules.reasoning: Severe breathing difficulty with red flags indicates respiratory distress requiring immediate emergency evaluation.

rules.title: Moderate breathing difficulty
follow_up_questions: When did the breathing difficulty start?
Can you identify any triggers (exertion, allergens, cold air)?
Do you have a history of asthma, allergies, or lung disease?
Do you have a fever along with the breathing difficulty?
rules.reasoning: Moderate breathing difficulty without severe red flags requires urgent evaluation but may not be immediately life-threatening.

rules.title: Breathing difficulty - insufficient information
follow_up_questions: When did the breathing difficulty start?
How severe is it on a scale of 1 to 10?
Can you speak in full sentences?
rules.reasoning: Breathing difficulty can range from mild to life-threatening. Insufficient information to determine severity.
escalation_conditions: patient unable to provide information due to distress
breathing difficulty with inability to speak

rules.title: Abdominal pain with surgical red flags
red_flags: inability to pass gas or stool
follow_up_questions: Where exactly is the pain located?
When did the pain start and how severe is it?
Have you noticed any blood in your stool or vomit?
Is your abdomen hard or rigid to the touch?
Are you able to pass gas or have a bowel movement?
rules.reasoning: Abdominal pain with red flags suggests possible surgical emergency requiring urgent evaluation.

rules.title: Abdominal pain without red flags
follow_up_questions: Where exactly is the pain located?
When did the pain start?
Can you describe the type of pain (cramping, sharp, burning)?
Do you have nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation?
rules.reasoning: Abdominal pain without red flags still requires evaluation but may be managed less urgently.
escalation_conditions: abdominal pain with unexplained weight loss

rules.title: Abdominal pain - insufficient information
follow_up_questions: Can you point to where the pain is?
When did the pain start?
Can you describe the type of pain?
rules.reasoning: Abdominal pain has wide differential. Insufficient information to determine severity or route safely.

rules.title: Fever combined with breathing difficulty - escalate
follow_up_questions: What is your current temperature?
How is your breathing right now? Are you short of breath?
Do you have a cough along with the fever?
rules.reasoning: Fever combined with breathing difficulty suggests possible pneumonia or serious respiratory infection requiring emergency evaluation.

rules.title: Conflicting or unclear symptom presentation
follow_up_questions: Can you describe your main concern more specifically?
When did these symptoms start?
Are you experiencing any other symptoms?
rules.reasoning: Symptom description is unclear or conflicting. Cannot determine appropriate triage category with confidence.
escalation_conditions: symptoms do not clearly match any category

rules.title: Complaint outside supported categories
rules.reasoning: The described complaint does not fall within the supported triage categories (fever, injury, chest pain, breathing difficulty, abdominal pain). This case should be reviewed by a human triage professional.
